batch_strategy: Measure controlled condition-response curves where observed endpoint behavior challenges structural transfer or the model's weak loading sensitivity. Complement these with a fluorinated hydrocarbon response curve, a matched loading-solvent comparison, and an uncovered acid extension. These 32 IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions are fixed before label revelation.

choices.reason: m128 at 5/1 and 50 mg predicts 17.10/33.14 mL. It fills the exact-loading gap before 2f72c334253bbe94a8ab at 10/1, measured at 39.47/54.40, and 55200f8e501a16ffa0cf at 20/1, 33.49/73.97. This localizes the onset transition separately from continued completion growth.

m128 at 5/1 and 150 mg predicts 17.10/33.16 mL and starts a matched higher-loading 5/1-to-10/1 pair. The 100 mg observations 892c3900698d3de38b1c and 92f7fe9d8581717a9949 established substantial growth. Together with the selected 50 mg 5/1 point, this checks the model's almost unchanged loading response.

m128 at 10/1 and 150 mg predicts 26.20/46.75 mL, below the measured 100 mg result in 92f7fe9d8581717a9949 and the 50 mg result in 2f72c334253bbe94a8ab. Its matched selected 5/1 point distinguishes a higher-loading association from insufficiently learned solvent-response growth; the prospective error remains unknown.

m107 at 5/1 and 163.5 mg predicts 39.11/84.95 mL. The lower-loading 5/1 observation c6924324ddd95f249df6 finished at 101.44 mL. Paired with the selected 2/1 point, this determines whether substantial growth persists at higher loading and supplies a constraint for related multifunctional acetoacetates.

m107 at 5/1 and 109 mg predicts 39.11/84.94 mL, essentially identical to the selected 163.5 mg forecast. The three-loading comparison with c6924324ddd95f249df6 tests whether its long completion is stable, loading-dependent, or variable beyond the available features. Observation 60b7eed7a46a03b366b2 supplies a matched 1/1 anchor.

Benzyl-substituted acetoacetate m78 at 10/1 and 155.4 mg predicts 12.74/24.05 mL. The 103.6 mg observation 3092a6310ab5c25cb83c was 12.52/27.13. This provides an intermediate anchor for the selected matched 50/1 extension, separating transition growth from loading transfer.

m78 at 50/1 and 155.4 mg predicts 40.05/71.41 mL. Observations 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760 and 61771d230b285babe4b6 finished at 97.46 and 97.97 mL at two lower loadings. This tests whether the shorter forecast represents a reproducible loading association and repairs transfer only if the new label warrants it.

Ethyl acetoacetate m82 at 10/1 and 154.35 mg predicts 15.55/34.13 mL. Observation 6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216 at 102.9 mg was 20.41/45.62. A matched selected 20/1 extension checks whether the current shorter endpoints reflect loading dependence or underlearned curvature in a common beta-ketoester.

m82 at 20/1 and 154.35 mg predicts 21.74/52.14 mL, versus 26.33/64.40 measured at 102.9 mg in 61090cfdcf019e0891a3. Measuring the matched 10/1-to-20/1 pair constrains onset and completion slopes while testing loading transfer, with direct relevance to the other acetoacetate panels.

Aryl beta-ketoester m81 at 20/1 and 111 mg predicts 7.64/17.70 mL. At this loading, fefecd79dc057980f62c and eb6c235e6ed90084bfc9 finished at 18.57 and 16.73 mL at 5/1 and 10/1. This tests an uncovered shallow extension and qualifies transfer of the steep aliphatic acetoacetate corrections.

Enamine ester m72 at 10/1, 102.2 mg, and 300 uL PE predicts 20.90/57.99 mL. It starts a matched PE-loaded 10/1-to-20/1 pair. The identical-condition lower-loading DCM outcomes in 7383949c431e18f39597 and 93bcd806b8dcb8c0cab9 were discordant, so this experiment tests transfer without assigning that variation to a loading law.

m72 at matched 20/1 predicts 31.36/107.22 mL. DCM-loaded observations 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d finished at 112.07 and 109.68 mL across loadings. This asks whether that stable late completion transfers to PE loading, with the selected 10/1 point identifying the intervening growth.

Para-nitroacetophenone m37 at 10/1 and 201.75 mg predicts 20.46/44.40 mL. Observation 38e6b8bf0f089fcadd80 at 134.5 mg was 25.64/55.08. This anchors a matched 10/1-to-20/1 pair to test loading transfer and the location of the strong completion rise.

m37 at 20/1 and 201.75 mg predicts 36.17/79.14 mL. The 134.5 mg observation b6f1b33a5491968c645e was 45.32/95.57. Its matched selected 10/1 point determines whether the lower forecast preserves the measured curve shape and provides a ketone comparator for the nitroaldehyde experiments.

Para-nitrobenzaldehyde m193 at 5/1 and 224.4 mg predicts 8.88/25.34 mL. The matched 2/1 observation ca5c649ce727f8a36f41 was 5.02/18.28. This fills the early portion of a matched 5/1-to-20/1 experiment, locating growth before the later response measured at another loading.

m193 at 20/1 and 224.4 mg predicts 30.65/70.10 mL. Observation c28747d70e7b51a1cc95 at 149.6 mg was 36.89/82.08. The selected matched 5/1 anchor tests transition shape and loading transfer, while comparison with m37 and m198 remains qualified by their differing injection conditions.

Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 10/1 and 150 mg predicts 14.55/33.62 mL. The 100 mg observations 4da6e3b93f29af1efa94 at 5/1 and 163874b97308a1ea2507 at 20/1 bracket substantial growth. This supplies an intermediate anchor for the selected exact-loading 50/1 extension.

m198 at 50/1 and 150 mg predicts 32.59/76.33 mL, below 41.16/92.81 measured at 100 mg in 8ab554cd154e9749790b. Together with its selected 10/1 point, this tests whether a shorter higher-loading curve is supported and constrains nitrocarbonyl transfer separately for both endpoints.

Tertiary alcohol m51 at 5/1 and 144.9 mg predicts 17.80/29.01 mL. This ratio is not covered by its measured 2/1 and 10/1 anchors, including 95a211366968c4cd1f0f and bad24d96575f423fe4fd. The matched selected 10/1 point tests where its sterically qualified alcohol response accelerates.

m51 at 10/1 and 144.9 mg predicts 37.58/64.85 mL, versus 30.62/58.17 measured at 96.6 mg in bad24d96575f423fe4fd. The selected 5/1-to-10/1 pair tests solvent-response shape and loading transfer without importing the nonmonotonic m207 loading pattern into all alcohols.

Benzylic secondary alcohol m61 at 5/1 and 101.2 mg predicts 6.12/12.25 mL. Observation 859ae738b615cf17b849 at matched 10/1 had early onset, 3.04/17.24. This tests whether the shallow forecast is a real structural counterexample to the later alcohol panels and constrains onset/completion decoupling.

Pentafluorobenzene m156 at 10/1 and 75.7 mg predicts 5.93/14.00 mL. Observation cd3c75eca39365e943e4 at matched 2/1 was 6.17/10.24. This starts a controlled 10/1, 20/1, 50/1 curve that tests the model's large predicted weak-eluent response for a molecule with no H-bond donor or acceptor.

m156 at matched 20/1 predicts 13.78/28.94 mL, a pronounced rise beyond the selected 10/1 forecast. Its CW distance percentile of 0.99847 flags an uncovered model-feature region. This intermediate label determines whether fluorination-associated curvature begins here; the chemical prior alone cannot decide that.

m156 at matched 50/1 predicts 25.04/50.58 mL with CW distance percentile 0.99962. Completing the three-point curve tests whether the predicted rise is genuine or excessive. A measured shallow result would constrain overgeneralization from polar weak-eluent compounds, while a steep result would teach an unusual structural relationship.

Biphenyl m210 at 50/1 and 150 mg predicts 10.19/21.82 mL. Observation a45500adef751d92ffd8 at matched 10/1 was 4.96/15.95. This provides an uncovered weak-eluent hydrocarbon reference for interpreting the m156 curve and learning when aromatic compounds without H-bonding groups still show endpoint growth.

Bromopropionic acid m45 at 50/1 and 170 mg predicts 29.86/75.96 mL. Matched observations d43d692e19100ebe5646 at 10/1 and e6605c23fb1943a6b848 at 20/1 were 14.79/32.17 and 26.49/57.16. This uncovered extension distinguishes further growth from saturation in an acid environment with a large historical completion underprediction.

Ortho-isopropylphenol m58 at 2/1 and 101.2 mg predicts 10.33/16.76 mL, later onset than its selected matched 5/1 forecast. Measuring the pair tests this predicted reversal in a phenol environment. Existing c023e9fab656fe2ce6a6 and 68a01853008546de06a1 establish the later 20/1-to-50/1 rise.

m58 at matched 5/1 predicts 8.51/16.03 mL. Paired with its selected 2/1 point, this determines whether the stronger-eluent onset decrease is reproducible or an interpolation artifact. The 10/1 lower-loading observation aafc5710406e440a4c8f supplies a nearby measured reference without establishing a matched-loading slope.

m9 at 50/1, 67.6 mg, and 300 uL DCM predicts 7.25/16.97 mL. Its selected PE counterpart changes only loading-solvent identity. The matched PE-versus-EA association in m92 observations e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2 and 95a3dcfe4436e929aa30 motivates testing solvent sensitivity in a different structural and mobile-phase environment.

m9 at the same 50/1 ratio, 67.6 mg, and 300 uL PE predicts 7.27/16.90 mL, effectively unchanged from its selected DCM counterpart. This controlled pair can teach either a loading-solvent effect under weak eluent or its absence for a hydrophobic analyte, qualifying transfer of solvent associations across catalog rows.

Para-methylacetophenone m32 at 20/1 and 100.4 mg predicts 8.37/18.44 mL. Observations 7522f965f25a50c9a3bc and 8dce8486dfe67a190d0d at lower and higher loading had onsets of 9.84 and 4.46 mL but similar completion near 20 mL. This third loading tests the endpoint-specific association and preserves a shallow counterexample to m128.

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl response corrections require structural and endpoint qualification. m128's completion continues growing from 10/1 to 20/1 even as onset moves earlier. m32 instead has a shallow or decreasing 20/1-to-50/1 completion response across observed loadings. Their loading associations should be tested separately rather than inferred from a carbonyl-wide rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest acquisition errors had opposite signs in these related ketones. Completing missing loading and transition anchors can repair steep sulfur-ketone responses while retaining constraints against excessive retention predictions for methylketones.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m128 preserve its 5/1-to-10/1 growth at 150 mg, where does the 50 mg transition begin, and does m32's middle-loading onset interpolate between its measured neighbors while completion remains similar?

hypotheses.content: Acetoacetate response depends on the carbonyl environment and substitution. m107, m82, and m78 show substantial ratio-dependent completion growth, whereas aryl beta-ketoester m81 has relatively shallow measured 5/1-to-10/1 completion. Several higher-loading forecasts lie below measured lower-loading endpoints, but whether this represents loading dependence or incomplete structural transfer remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These experiments distinguish steep curves from shallow structural neighbors and test the predictor's nearly invariant loading forecasts. The labels can generalize across multiple beta-ketoester condition grids without relying on carbonyl count alone.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m107, m82, and m78 curves retain their measured completion growth at higher loading, and does m81 remain shallow through 20/1?

hypotheses.content: m72's long 20/1 completion is supported across two DCM-loaded sample amounts, while its identical-condition 10/1 observations at lower loading are discordant. A single monotonic loading or loading-solvent explanation is therefore unresolved. The matched PE-loaded 10/1-to-20/1 pair tests transfer of the more stable completion feature.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs condition-qualified nitrogen response curves and a distinction between patterns explained by recorded features and variation within identical feature tuples. The selected pair adds an interpretable curve under one fixed injection condition.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 102.2 mg with PE loading, is completion near the measured approximately 110 mL DCM-loaded 20/1 regime, and how much growth occurs from 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Nitrocarbonyl compounds have structure-specific solvent-response transitions: m37 and m193 rise substantially from 10/1 to 20/1, while m198 grows further toward 50/1. The much earlier nitroarene m201 response qualifies transfer through the nitro group alone. Stability of the carbonyl curves at the selected higher loadings remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched extensions can establish whether current shorter forecasts are supported by loading associations and can locate onset and completion transitions separately. Comparing ketone and aldehyde environments tests qualified transfer across many aromatic polar rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected higher-loading m37, m193, and m198 pairs preserve the measured transition locations and endpoint growth, allowing for their different recorded injection conditions?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl-containing compounds do not support a shared loading law or retention shift. m119's late 5/1 response persists at higher loading, whereas m207's three 5/1 outcomes are nonmonotonic in loading. The measured m51, m61, and m58 anchors suggest different onset/completion relationships across tertiary alcohol, benzylic alcohol, and phenol environments; their missing transition segments need direct measurement.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected alcohol and phenol experiments can constrain structural transfer while retaining measured early-onset counterexamples. They also test a predicted local reversal without imposing solvent monotonicity as an absolute rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m51's 5/1-to-10/1 growth occur at higher loading, does m61 remain early at 5/1, and is m58's predicted 2/1-to-5/1 onset decrease observed?

hypotheses.content: The model's steep weak-eluent response for pentafluorobenzene m156 may be excessive, but its zero TPSA and lack of H-bonding groups do not establish early elution at every ratio. The measured 2/1 anchor is early; the selected 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 curve tests whether the later predicted regime exists. Biphenyl supplies a qualified hydrocarbon comparison.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This explores a scarcely measured weak-eluent feature region where the predictor forecasts a large change for an acceptor-free structure. Either outcome can qualify transfer from polar compounds and improve fluorinated-aromatic predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m156 show the predicted progressive endpoint rise beyond 10/1, and how does its weak-eluent behavior compare with the selected biphenyl extension?

hypotheses.content: Loading-solvent associations may depend on both molecule and mobile-phase strength. Matched m92 observations at 1/1 differ between PE and EA loading, motivating a PE-versus-DCM test for hydrophobic m9 at 50/1. The current predictor gives essentially identical endpoints for the m9 pair; a comparable measured effect is not established.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Changing only loading-solvent identity provides a direct constraint on a condition feature that otherwise confounds many structural comparisons. A small effect is also informative if it limits inappropriate transfer of solvent associations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched 67.6 mg, 300 uL loading volume, and 50/1 mobile phase, do PE and DCM loading materially change either m9 endpoint?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels further reject carbonyl-wide or hydroxyl-wide corrections. m128's 50 mg completion increased from 54.40 mL at 10/1 to 73.97 mL at 20/1 while onset decreased, so the earlier saturation hypothesis remains rejected. m32's higher-loading completion instead fell from 20.35 to 14.24 mL across 20/1-to-50/1; this reinforces structural qualification and motivates one middle-loading onset anchor. m127's low-loading endpoints also decreased across that extension, resembling the higher-loading ordering, but its nearly coincident 109 mg endpoints did not recur. Its measured weak-eluent grid now offers more value as a constraint than as a reason for further stronger-eluent sampling. m207's new 78 mg 5/1 result, 21.18/34.03 mL, weakens a monotonic loading explanation and leaves the unusually early 156 mg outcome unresolved. Conversely, m119's higher-loading 5/1 result reproduced late elution closely enough to reduce further allocation there. Nitrogen feedback remains environment-specific: m90 completion was underpredicted at 10/1 by 23.65 mL, meta-aminobenzoate completion at 5/1 by 19.58 mL, and dibenzylamine completion at 5/1 by 20.15 mL, whereas ortho-aminobenzoate at 10/1 was earlier than forecast. This supports qualified transition experiments rather than a common upward nitrogen correction. m168's nearly fixed onset and modest completion growth support a shallow intermediate curve, with no measured onset reversal. The nitrile 10/1 anchors and benzyl-benzoate 50/1 result substantially complete their previous local questions, so they receive no additional allocation. Observed-table mappings correct two memory errors: c6924324ddd95f249df6 is m107 at 5/1, and 6d7b9c18dcb836a2b09c is m182, not a matched m181 lactone anchor. Historical errors here are acquisition-time errors; no candidate error is treated as measured.
batch_rationale: The batch contains ten matched within-molecule solvent-response pairs, one matched three-ratio m156 curve, and one matched PE-versus-DCM loading comparison. Seven additional anchors fill specific loading or response gaps. The carbonyl and acetoacetate panels target demonstrated failure regions while retaining shallow measured neighbors that prevent broad upward corrections. The nitrocarbonyl and hydroxyl panels test structural qualification and loading transfer at fixed recorded injection conditions. m72 receives a controlled curve because its stable late completion and discordant identical-condition intermediate labels require different interpretations. The m156 curve explores a chemically surprising prediction in a distant model-feature region, with biphenyl providing a useful structural reference; m45 adds an uncovered acid extension. Allocation is limited where recent labels completed a question or exposed variation that the available features may not explain. These measurements should constrain relationships shared across catalog condition grids and improve both endpoint targets after retraining, rather than pursue extreme elution volumes. Cross-molecule comparisons remain conditional on their recorded loadings and injection conditions. Sample amounts are density-times-volume features. Quantile spans and CW distance are secondary model-behavior evidence, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 remains the elution interval width.
